summary: Observation of aircraft evolution
description: On November 24, 1996, around 4:00 PM, a witness observed bright lights and objects moving in the sky. Another witness, contacted by the first, observed the phenomenon and clearly identified it as the flight of aircraft, which are very common in the area. It was therefore a case of mistaken identity.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On November 22, 1996, at approximately 6:00 AM, a witness observed the very rapid passage of a luminous sphere with a trail. The phenomenon described was likely an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of the very rapid passage of a luminous object with a significant trail
description: On November 5, 1996, two witnesses observed the very rapid passage of a cylindrical luminous phenomenon with a significant trail. No sound was heard. No other information could be gathered. It should be noted, however, that the observation site is near Lille airport and that the observed phenomenon followed the same flight path as airliners.

summary: Recent testimony of an old observation of lights forming a stationary triangle then moving at variable speed in the sky: lack of information.
description: On October 20, 2010, GEIPAN received a report from someone concerning an earlier sighting that occurred at 9:00 PM in late October 1996 (the witness did not specify the exact date, so October 30th was arbitrarily given). Then 11 years old, the witness, accompanied by his mother and younger brother, was initially intrigued by the sight of three stationary lights above the trees in a square in Angers. The witness then described the phenomenon as a triangle with a black circle in the center that moved and disappeared with a sudden acceleration. No noise was heard during the 20-second observation. The second witness (the mother) recalled a sighting in the fall of 1996 around 8:00 PM of an unusual light and a moving object that she did not recognize. No other reports were collected regarding this phenomenon. The description of this case is too imprecise (incomplete date) and too old for GEIPAN to investigate and a fortiori to make a decision on this case, class "C", due to lack of information.

summary: Successive observations of luminous phenomena during a car journey in the early morning: lack of information.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named CORME ROYAL (17) 1996, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined (see the investigation report). On September 16, 1996, at around 5:00 a.m., a witness was driving to work. During his journey (observation point 0), he suddenly noticed a rather large and brightly lit point of light. A few kilometers further on (observation point 1), he noticed on his left side a stationary ovoid craft with three square portholes emitting a strong orange light. The witness continued on his way and, near Saintes (observation point 2), observed two shapes in the sky identical to his second observation. Only one testimony was collected. The very first part of the observation (observation point 0), which the witness described as follows: "I first noticed a rather large point in the sky, which emitted a bright luminosity, while I was driving towards Nancras. I was intrigued by its strong brightness and its quite unusual size." The witness probably observed the planet Venus, rising in the east-northeast, that is, facing its direction of movement. The police report mentions the presence of a radio relay station with three orange lights (the witness describes three portholes), and another antenna. Both are visible from observation point 2, but not from observation point 1, even though the witness seems to see the same characteristics. This doesn't appear to be the explanation. For observation point 1, there is no explanatory hypothesis. The witness's description of the UFO, and its apparent immobility, do not allow for any explanatory hypothesis. Furthermore, the data collected during the witness's interview is insufficient in quality and reliability. A nighttime reconstruction on site would have allowed for angle measurements (position and angular width), more extensive and precise questioning of the witness, and further investigation of existing hypotheses, perhaps even the development of new ones. More than 20 years later, relaunching such an investigation seems futile. Based on the current A/B/C/D1/D2 classification methodology (see the explanations on the GEIPAN classification methodology), the present case would be classified as D1 strange, but its consistency is too weak to validate the unexplained nature of the observation. Consequently, the case is classified as C due to a lack of reliable information.

summary: Observations by two witnesses of a circular object (skirt surmounted by a cylinder) with colored lights and a green flash. Stationary near the ground then moving silently; disappearance as the UFO moved away: unidentified phenomenon.
description: This case was previously published under the name Pont-De-Salars (12). On September 12, 1996, around 8:00 PM, a mother and daughter driving near Flavin (12) observed an object they could not identify. The craft consisted of an ovoid skirt and a cylinder topped with a bright red dome (with three lights). A fluorescent green light on the cylinder rotated like a flashing beacon. The silent object hovered approximately 4 meters above the ground, about 10 meters from the road. Its size was compared to that of about two cars. After a few minutes, the object moved away to the north or northwest. That same evening, after the observation, each witness made a drawing and took notes. The following day, they were interviewed at the gendarmerie. The observation was estimated to have lasted approximately two minutes. A computer-aided drawing was created by a police officer based on information from witnesses. The on-site investigation failed to uncover any traces or clues. On the evening of the observation, the sky was clear and starry, and there was no wind. Air traffic and radar indicated no unusual activity. Surveillance patrols were conducted in the following days but revealed nothing. Searches for other eyewitness accounts in the vicinity were unsuccessful. No similar cases were reported in the print or television media. From the police investigation and the witnesses' descriptions of the phenomenon, no coherent explanation could be found. The phenomenon remains unexplained.

summary: An orange ball was observed flying over the trees.
description: During the night of September 6-7, 1996, a witness at a sanatorium observed an orange ball descending slowly from the sky and flying over the trees around 2:00 AM. No further information was gathered about this sighting.

summary: Observation of several bright points in the sky
description: On August 31, 1996, at approximately 10:15 PM, a witness observed several bright points of light for an hour, which he did not identify as stars. No further information is available.

summary: Likely sighting of a disco projector
description: On August 11, 1996, between 12:30 and 1:30 AM, a witness and his wife observed a circular luminous phenomenon moving slowly from right to left. They observed this phenomenon for approximately 45 minutes and went to bed while it was still present. The investigation revealed that the direction of the observation corresponded to that of a nightclub using a laser advertising projector. The observed phenomenon was therefore likely the effect of this projector on the clouds.

summary: Likely sighting of an advertising laser projector
description: On August 9, 1996, four witnesses observed lights moving in a circle at high speed between 2:30 and 3:30 a.m. The investigation and witness statements indicated that this was likely the effect of a laser projector used during a festival in a nearby village.

summary: Probable observations of atmospheric reentry.
description: On the evening of August 1, 1996, numerous witnesses observed the very rapid passage of a very bright white sphere with a yellow and green trail. The luminous phenomenon lasted approximately thirty seconds. It was described in the same terms from Cantal to Alsace. The times given varied slightly, but the phenomenon appears to have occurred between 9:30 p.m. and 9:45 p.m., moving towards the Northwest. This large-scale phenomenon, seen by many witnesses in eastern France, was probably an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of a bright point
description: On July 3, 1996, just before midnight, a witness observing the sky saw a bright point flash briefly (15 seconds) at high speed. No further information is available, but the description suggests a minor atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of orange glows in the sky
description: On May 20, 1996, at approximately 11:45 PM, a witness was drawn by the sound of barking dogs. For several dozen seconds, he observed orange lights moving slowly, accompanied by two rows of orange and blue lights. No noise was detected. No other information is available.

summary: Observation of a cylindrical object
description: On April 20, 1996, at approximately 10:20 PM, a witness observed a cylindrical flying object from their apartment, with flashing lights underneath. The object was silent and moved more slowly than an airplane. Its straight trajectory then became upward after a 180-degree turn. The total duration of the observation was approximately 10 minutes. No further information is available regarding this case.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On April 8, 1996, a witness in a car observed a fireball with a trail falling towards the ground for a few moments. The phenomenon was silent, and the fireball suddenly extinguished, turning a dark red. The witness's description corresponds to the observation of atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a very bright point of light above the horizon
description: On April 1, 1995, at 11:40 PM, a witness observed a bright point of light on the horizon while returning home. The light moved very slowly. This observation lasted approximately 50 minutes. The witness filmed the phenomenon, which did indeed show a very bright white point. There is too little information about this phenomenon to draw any conclusions.

summary: Observation of traces on astronomical photographs
description: On March 27, 1996, an astronomy enthusiast noticed dark streaks in photographs of a comet, the origin of which he could not explain. The photos were of limited use, and no conclusions could be drawn.

summary: Observation of slowly moving white lights for 40 minutes
description: On March 9, 1996, at approximately 9:20 PM, a private pilot observed one or two white lights, along with a green and a red light, moving for about 40 minutes. These lights were followed by a luminous trail. The witness immediately alerted the police, but the phenomenon had disappeared by the time they arrived around 10:15 PM. No further information could be obtained.

summary: Likely observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On March 1, 1996, at approximately 7:30 PM, four witnesses observed a very bright point moving across the sky with a white trail, making the whole thing resemble a neon tube. The phenomenon was silent and lasted between one and three minutes. It was most likely the atmospheric reentry of a meteorite or space debris.

summary: Observation of a bright point in the sky
description: On February 10, 1996, at approximately 8:00 PM, a witness, his wife, and his son observed a very bright point in the sky, its diameter significantly larger than that of a star. A second point was also observed. The witness filmed the observation, but the information is too limited to analyze the phenomenon.

summary: Observing a casino projector
description: On January 9, 1996, around 8 p.m., several witnesses observed large luminous circles with numerous points of light inside. These circles rotated in the sky. The investigation revealed that this phenomenon was caused by the reflection of a spotlight from a nearby casino off the clouds.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous phenomenon.
description: Recent testimony (September 2, 2009) of an earlier observation (in 1996, give or take two years; the date and month given here are arbitrary as they were not precisely indicated by the witness). Around 7:00 PM, a motorist and his daughter observed a white halo, 80 cm by 40 cm, moving at a constant speed. The witness noted a peculiar trajectory made up of straight segments at a constant speed and 1.5 meters above the ground. Moving from north to south, the object made a sudden turn to the west. No noise was heard during the observation, which lasted approximately one minute. No other testimonies were collected regarding this phenomenon, for which, given its age, any investigation is difficult, if not impossible.
